what_its_for: Metyrosine is used to treat a tumor of the adrenal gland called pheochromocytoma. This tumor causes your body to release too much of certain stress hormones (like adrenaline), which can cause dangerously high blood pressure, rapid heartbeat, and other serious problems. Metyrosine works by blocking the production of these hormones, helping to lower your blood pressure and reduce symptoms before, during, or instead of surgery.
how_to_take: Take metyrosine by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. You may take it with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time. Drink plenty of fluids throughout the day — at least 6 to 8 full glasses of water or other liquids daily — unless your doctor tells you otherwise. This helps prevent kidney stones, which can be a side effect of this medicine.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 250 mg (one capsule) taken 4 times a day. Your doctor may gradually increase your dose up to a maximum of 4,000 mg (4 grams) per day, depending on how your body responds and how well your symptoms are controlled. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store metyrosine capsules at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed and away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use medicine that is expired — check the expiration date on the bottle and safely dispose of any unused or outdated medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metyrosine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Be careful when driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing any activity that requires you to be alert, because this medicine can cause significant drowsiness and slow your thinking. Avoid getting up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as metyrosine can cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Tell all of your healthcare providers (including dentists) that you take this medicine before any procedure or surgery.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: severe or unusual muscle stiffness, tremors, or uncontrolled movements; difficulty speaking or swallowing; high fever; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing; signs of kidney stones such as severe back or side pain, pain when urinating, or blood in your urine; extreme drowsiness or confusion; or if your blood pressure symptoms seem to be getting worse. Also contact your doctor if you notice any new or worsening side effects.
when_it_works: Metyrosine usually starts working within a few days of starting treatment. However, it may take 1 to 3 weeks to see the full benefit, such as better blood pressure control and reduction in symptoms like headache, sweating, or rapid heartbeat. Your doctor will monitor your hormone levels and blood pressure regularly to check how well the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): You may be more sensitive to side effects like drowsiness and dizziness. Use caution and talk to your doctor about the right dose for you. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not known if metyrosine is safe during pregnancy or if it passes into breast milk — your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits with you. Kidney problems: Metyrosine is removed from the body by the kidneys. If you have kidney disease or reduced kidney function, your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely. Children: Use in children under 12 years old has not been well studied. Your doctor will determine if this medicine is appropriate for your child.
